simple.meaning: פֶּרֶץ (perets) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a break (literally or figuratively).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 19 times in Genesis, Judges, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, 1 Chronicles, and 6 more, beginning at Genesis 38:29. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, kingship, city, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פֶּרֶץ (H6556) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: פֶּרֶץ (perets) / H6556 is traced through Genesis 38:29, Judges 21:15, 2 Samuel 5:20, 2 Samuel 6:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6556. perets I. מֶּ֫רֶץ noun masculine Job 30:14 bursting forth, breach ; absolute ׳פ Judg 21:15 +, מָּ֑רֶץ Gen 38:29 +; construct מֶּרֶץ 2Sam 5:20 +; plural מְּרָצִים Amos 4:3 +, מְּרָצוֺם Ezek 13:5 , suffix מִּרְצֵיהֶץ Amos 9:11 ( מְּרָצֶיהָ We Now); — 1 bursting forth, out burst , of water 2Sam 5:20 = 1Chr 14:11 ; from womb Gen 38:29 (J). 2 breach in wall Amos 4:3 ; 1Kin 11:27 ; Neh 6:1 ; Psa 144:14 ; Job 30:14 ; so (with גָּדַר , i.e. repair) Amos 9:11 ; Isa 58:12 ; figurative of effect to avert calamity, בַּמְּרָצוֺת עָלָה Ezek 13:5 (|| גָּדַר ), בַּמֶּרֶץ עָמַד 22:30 (|| id.), compare Psa 106:23 , by instruction and (especially) intercession. 3 broken wall , ׳פ נֹפֵל Isa 30:13 . 4 figurative of outburst of ׳י s wrath, accusative of congnate meaning with verb with מָּרַץ 2Sam 6:8 = 1Chr 13:11 ; Job 16:14 ( עַלמְּֿנֵיפָֿ֑רֶץ מֶּרֶץ ); פ ׳עָשָׂה בְּ Judg 21:15 .

occurrences.englishText: As he drew back his hand, behold, his brother came out, and she said, “Why have you made a breach for yourself?” Therefore his name was called Perez.* Perez means “breaking out”.
The people grieved for Benjamin, because Yahweh had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.

David came to Baal Perazim, and David struck them there. Then he said, “Yahweh has broken my enemies before me, like the breach of waters.” Therefore he called the name of that place Baal Perazim.* “Baal Perazim” means “Lord who breaks out”.
David was displeased, because Yahweh had broken out against Uzzah; and he called that place Perez Uzzah,* “Perez Uzzah” means “outbreak against Uzzah”. to this day.
This was the reason why he lifted up his hand against the king: Solomon built Millo, and repaired the breach of his father David’s city.
David was displeased, because Yahweh had broken out against Uzza. He called that place Perez Uzza, to this day.

So they came up to Baal Perazim, and David defeated them there. David said, God has broken my enemies by my hand, like waters breaking out. Therefore they called the name of that place Baal Perazim.* “Baal Perazim” means “The Lord who breaks out”.

Now when it was reported to Sanballat, Tobiah, and to Geshem the Arabian, and to the rest of our enemies, that I had built the wall, and that there was no breach left in it (though even to that time I had not set up the doors in the gates)
He breaks me with breach on breach.
He breaks me with breach on breach.
As through a wide breach they come.
Therefore he said that he would destroy them,
Our oxen will pull heavy loads.
therefore this iniquity shall be to you like a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking comes suddenly in an instant.
Those who will be of you will build the old waste places.
You have not gone up into the gaps or built up the wall for the house of Israel, to stand in the battle in Yahweh’s day.
“I sought for a man among them who would build up the wall and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I would not destroy it; but I found no one.
You will go out at the breaks in the wall,
In that day I will raise up the tent of David who is fallen, and close up its breaches, and I will raise up its ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old;
